'''Amanohashidate Shrine''' (あまのはしだてじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Higashimiyoshi|Q1206006|qid=Q1206006}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|Q160734|qid=Q160734}}.

=== History ===
The year of foundation is unknown. Until the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was called Hazu Myōjin. The reason it was called “Hazu Myōjin” is unknown. According to the *Miyoshi District Gazetteer*, the entire area currently known as Miyauchi constituted the shrine precincts, and the place 100 meters south of the shrine was called “Torii,” where the foundation stones of an actual torii gate once existed.

It is one of the candidate shrines (ronsha) for Amanohashidate Shrine, which is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* {{ill|Izanagi|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q813858}}
* {{ill|Izanami|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto|qid=Q682306}}

=== Access ===
* About 10 minutes by car from “{{ill|Tsuji Station|Q577894|qid=Q577894}}” on the {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|Q496531|qid=Q496531|lt=JR}} {{ill|Tokushima Line|Q899310|qid=Q899310}}.
